ca_falls_walls.blurb: Falls Walls is a cluster of three small, separate walls within the Indian Springs area, sitting between the main lower cliffs and the Johnny Wall. Nine routes climb here, eight bolted and one on gear, from easy fifth class up to 5.12, with the biggest share in the 5.10 range. Routes are short and tend to feel true to their grades, so a party can work through most or all of them in a single afternoon. The faces are well featured. A seasonal waterfall runs down beside the bolted lines on the right-hand wall.

ca_fortress_the_3.blurb: The Fortress is a steep, blocky cliff in the Benches section of The Emeralds, on the terrace directly above Steel Monkey Wall. All nine routes are bolted sport lines, and none is a beginner option: three are 5.10, four are 5.11 and two are 5.12. It suits climbers who are already comfortable on steep, hard face climbing. Because several other Benches walls sit on neighbouring terraces, it is easy to pair this cliff with another wall during the same visit.

ca_noir_boulder_the.blurb: The Noir Boulder is a large, well-featured river boulder in the Santa Barbara bouldering zone, with a few much smaller blocks close by. Nine problems climb the sandstone, ranging from V2 up to V11, so the grades lean toward strong climbers and the easiest lines are few. Landings are generally fine, but the topouts are airy and can be mossy, so brush off the exits before committing. The volume of problems is small, and the hardest lines are still open projects.

ca_main_wall_16.blurb: Main Wall is a large south-facing formation at Corte Madera in San Diego County, with both traditional and sport multi-pitch routes. Nine climbs are on the wall: five bolted and four on gear, nearly all between 5.10 and 5.11 with a single 5.8. The gear routes can involve some bushwhacking along the way, while the bolted lines follow cleaner faces. Most parties reach the base by hiking to the top and rappelling in, though a long walk up from below is also an option.

ca_fallout_zone_the.blurb: The Fallout Zone is a short wall of basalt in Warner Valley in the Lassen area, directly above and behind the Loading Zone crag, so both are easy to visit in one day. It is vertical to overhanging and well featured, with a black-and-white streaked face. Nine routes climb it, eight bolted and one trad, from 5.9 to 5.12 with 5.10 the most common grade. Each line has its own anchors, and the top can be reached to set up a toprope.

ca_dos_equis_boulder.blurb: Dos Equis Boulder is a large block with a big face, sitting toward the back of the circuit in the Descanso Boulders, a small bouldering zone in San Diego County. Nine climbs are here: five low-grade problems from V0 to V2, three trad leads and one toprope between 5.10 and 5.11. The rock is heavily featured, and shade is scarce except behind the taller boulders. Blocks in the zone stand from about 6 feet to 35 feet or more. Trails are still being developed, so the route in can be hard to follow.
